draft.title: Polar form
card: Polar form writes a complex number as z = r cis θ, where r is the modulus and θ is the argument. cis θ means cos θ + i sin θ.
To convert from a + bi, find r = √(a² + b²) and the angle θ from the position of the point. For example, 1 + i = √2 cis(π/4).
To multiply, multiply the moduli and add the arguments: (r₁ cis θ₁)(r₂ cis θ₂) = r₁r₂ cis(θ₁ + θ₂).
Example: (2 cis(π/6))(3 cis(π/3)) = 6 cis(π/6 + π/3) = 6 cis(π/2), which is 6i.
draft.remember: To multiply in polar form, multiply the moduli and add the arguments.

a.q: What is (4 cis(π/5))(2 cis(π/10)) in polar form?
a.why: Multiply the moduli: 4 × 2 = 8. Add the arguments: π/5 + π/10 = 2π/10 + π/10 = 3π/10. Adding the moduli instead is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Moduli are multiplied. Arguments are added.

b.q: What is 3 cis(2π/3) × 2 cis(π/2) written with its argument in the range −π < θ ≤ π?
b.why: The modulus is 3 × 2 = 6. The arguments add to 2π/3 + π/2 = 7π/6, which is above π. Subtract 2π to get −5π/6. The option 6 cis(7π/6) is correct as a value but its argument is outside the range.
b.clue: After adding, check whether the angle is bigger than π.

problems.detail: The question needs students to know that the principal argument lies in −π < θ ≤ π and that you subtract 2π to bring an angle into that range. The card never mentions the range or this adjustment. Only the clue hints at it.

proposal.title: Polar form
card: Polar form writes a complex number as z = r cis θ, where r is the modulus and θ is the argument. cis θ means cos θ + i sin θ.
To convert from a + bi, find r = √(a² + b²) and the angle θ from the position of the point. For example, 1 + i = √2 cis(π/4).
To multiply, multiply the moduli and add the arguments: (r₁ cis θ₁)(r₂ cis θ₂) = r₁r₂ cis(θ₁ + θ₂). For example, (2 cis(π/6))(3 cis(π/3)) = 6 cis(π/2), which is 6i.
The principal argument lies in the range −π < θ ≤ π. If a sum of arguments falls outside it, add or subtract 2π, which gives the same point. For example, cis(5π/4) = cis(−3π/4).

final.title: Polar form
card: Polar form writes a complex number as \(z = r\,\text{cis}\,\theta\), where \(r\) is the modulus and \(\theta\) is the argument. \(\text{cis}\,\theta\) means \(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta\).
To convert from \(a + bi\), find \(r = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\) and the angle \(\theta\) from the position of the point. For example, \(1 + i = \sqrt{2}\,\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).

To multiply, multiply the moduli and add the arguments: \((r_{1}\,\text{cis}\,\theta_{1})(r_{2}\,\text{cis}\,\theta_{2}) = r_{1}r_{2}\,\text{cis}(\theta_{1} + \theta_{2})\). For example, \(\left(2\,\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\left(3\,\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = 6\,\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), which is \(6i\).

The principal argument lies in the range \(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\). If a sum of arguments falls outside it, add or subtract \(2\pi\), which gives the same point. For example, \(\text{cis}\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}\right) = \text{cis}\left(-\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\).
final.remember: Multiply the moduli, add the arguments, then add or subtract \(2\pi\) if the angle leaves the range \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\).

a.why: Multiply the moduli: \(4 \times 2 = 8\). Add the arguments: \(\frac{\pi}{5} + \frac{\pi}{10} = \frac{2\pi}{10} + \frac{\pi}{10} = \frac{3\pi}{10}\). Adding the moduli or multiplying the arguments are the tempting mistakes.
a.clue: Moduli are multiplied. Arguments are added.

b.q: What is \(3\,\text{cis}\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) \times 2\,\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) written with its argument in the range \(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)?
b.why: The modulus is \(3 \times 2 = 6\). The arguments add to \(\frac{2\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{7\pi}{6}\), which is above \(\pi\), so subtract \(2\pi\) to get \(-\frac{5\pi}{6}\). The option \(6\,\text{cis}\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\) is the same number, but its argument is outside the range asked for.
b.clue: After adding, check whether the angle is bigger than \(\pi\).
